column2: Og and all his people meet Israel for battle at Edrei after its turn toward Bashan; every participant and location remains.
Fear is forbidden because Og, his people and his land are delivered, with Sihon at Heshbon as the explicit precedent.
The Lord delivers Og and his people, and none of his seed remains after the attack; the selected seed expression is preserved.
All sixty cities in Argob of Og's Bashan kingdom are taken; the negative no city untaken and the positive total both remain.
High walls, gates and bars describe the fortified cities, besides very many Perizzite cities; the selected ethnic designation is not changed to unwalled villages.
Every city in succession, women and children are destroyed as in Sihon's case, retaining the repeated destruction and violent scope.
Propose livestock for cattle to preserve the generic ktene in this plunder list. All, city spoil and for ourselves remain.
The land taken from the two Amorite kings extends from Arnon to Hermon beyond Jordan.
Phoenicians call Hermon Sanior and Amorites call it Senir; both selected names and their naming groups remain distinct.
Misor, Gilead and Bashan extend to Salcah and Edrei, identified as Og's kingdom cities.
Og alone remains of the Rephaim; his iron bed is in Ammon's citadel and measures nine by four human cubits. Neither the citadel nor measurements are harmonized.
Aroer at Arnon and half Gilead with its towns are assigned to Reuben and Gad after the inheritance statement.
The remaining Gilead and all Bashan/Argob go to half Manasseh; the classification as Rephaim land remains.
Jair's Argob territory reaches Gargasi and the Maacathites; the naming after himself and its continuation until today remain.
column3: The selected Omachathi is conventionally represented by Maacathites; fuller name-authority and geographical review remain open.

column2: Machir receives Gilead in a brief separate allotment statement.
Reuben and Gad receive territory to Arnon's middle and to Jabbok, the boundary for Ammon; both watercourse limits remain.
Arabah, Jordan, Machanareth, the Salt Sea and eastern Asedoth-Pisgah remain in the selected boundary sequence.
column3: The compressed boundary syntax and Machanareth's relationship to Jordan require geographical and grammatical review; no familiar alternative is substituted.

column2: Every able man must go armed before Israel's brothers after receiving this land; both gift and obligation remain.
Propose livestock in both occurrences of cattle, preserving the generic animal term and the parenthetical recognition of its abundance. Wives and children remain separate groups.
The brothers' rest and western inheritance precede each man's return; selected your God and our God remain in their respective clauses.
Joshua receives the command, while the initial your eyes is plural in Greek and the final you crossing is singular; English you preserves wording without adding all.
The plural prohibition of fear is grounded in the Lord Himself fighting for the addressed people.
Moses' entreaty introduces direct divine address.
Repeated Lord, strength, power, mighty hand and uplifted arm remain; Thou hast and Thy/Thine follow the divine-address rule without adding archaic forms elsewhere.
The request seeks crossing and sight of the good land, good hills and Anti-Lebanon; the inherited petition renders the contextual force of the future clause.
Propose because of you for for your sakes to clarify the causal heneken phrase. The selected disregarded verb, refusal to hear and command to speak no more remain.
The summit is the Hewn Place, not a substituted familiar proper name; sea, north, southwest and east are all retained before the refusal of crossing.
Commanding, strengthening and encouraging Joshua are distinct; he leads the crossing and enables inheritance of what Moses has seen.
The valley near the house of Peor closes the narrative setting, retaining the descriptive house expression.
Hearing and doing ordinances and judgments lead to life, multiplication, entry and inheritance; all stated purposes remain.
Neither addition nor subtraction is permitted, and the Lord's commandments given today must be kept.
Israel has seen the Lord's action concerning Baal-peor, and every follower is removed from among them; both sight and judgment remain.
Those attached to the Lord are all alive today, preserving the contrast with the previous judgment.
Moses has shown ordinances and judgments as commanded for practice in the inherited land.
Keeping and doing the ordinances displays wisdom and understanding before all nations, whose quoted recognition remains.
The rhetorical question concerns a god drawing near as the Lord does when called upon, preserving nearness and invocation.
A second question concerns righteous ordinances and judgments matching this entire law set before Israel today.
Diligent self-guarding, lifelong remembrance and instruction of sons and grandsons remain, with the sentence continuing into the remembered day.
The Horeb assembly hears the Lord's words to learn lifelong fear and teach its children; the selected day of assembly remains explicit.
The people stand beneath the burning mountain, with darkness, gloom, tempest and great sound all retained.
They hear words from fire but see no likeness, only a voice; the selected contrast is preserved without inventing a visible form.
The covenant is the ten words commanded for performance and written on two stone tablets; both counts remain.
Moses is commanded to teach ordinances and judgments for practice in the land Israel is entering.
Guarding their souls is grounded in seeing no likeness when the Lord spoke from fire at Horeb.
Lawlessness through making a carved likeness is prohibited, including male and female images.
Earthly animals and winged birds beneath heaven extend the likeness prohibition, keeping the broad animal category in this context.
Creeping things on earth and fish in waters beneath earth complete the listed creature likenesses.
Sun, moon, stars and heaven's adornment must not lead Israel into worship and service; their allotment to nations remains stated without theological expansion.
God takes Israel out of Egypt's iron furnace as a people of inheritance; the source's furnace metaphor remains.
Anger concerns the things spoken by Israel, and the oath excludes Moses from both Jordan crossing and entry; the selected verbal cause is retained.
Moses' death in this land contrasts with Israel's crossing and inheritance of the good land.
Forgetting the covenant and making a likeness are prohibited; concerning which the Lord has given commandment retains the selected relative wording without adding a new negative inside it.
Consuming fire and jealous God remain the two characterizations, without softened imagery.
Generations, long residence, lawless image-making and provoking the Lord form the conditional warning.
Heaven and earth witness the warning of destruction, no long duration and utter removal from the land; repeated emphatic destruction remains.
Scattering among all nations leaves few in number where the Lord brings them; both agency and diminished number remain.
Wood-and-stone gods made by human hands cannot see, hear, eat or smell; all four negated abilities remain.
Seeking and finding the Lord requires whole heart and soul amid distress; distress remains attached here in the selected numbering.
All these things find Israel in the latter days, followed by return and hearing the Lord's voice.
The merciful Lord will neither forsake nor destroy nor forget the ancestral covenant; all three negatives remain.
Inquiry extends from human creation and across heaven's ends, asking whether anything comparable has happened or been heard.
A nation hearing the living God's voice from fire and surviving forms the next rhetorical question.
Trial, signs, wonders, war, mighty hand, uplifted arm and great visions all remain in the exodus question; selected visions is not changed to terrors.
The purpose is recognition that the Lord is God with none beside Him, retaining the exclusive conclusion.
His voice becomes audible from heaven for instruction, while the great fire is shown on earth and words heard from it; the selected voice construction remains.
Love of the fathers, choice of their descendants identified as you, and personal deliverance from Egypt by great strength remain connected.
Destroying greater nations, bringing Israel in and giving their land explain the deliverance, with the present possession acknowledged.
Today's recognition and inward consideration concern the Lord as God above and below, with none beside Him.
Keeping ordinances and commands serves the welfare of Israel and its descendants and long life in the given land.
column3: For ever renders the selected all the days idiom; its temporal nuance and attachment remain open for the fuller lexical review.

column2: Moses sets apart three cities east of Jordan, preserving the sunrise orientation.
Unintentional killing without prior hatred permits refuge and continued life; both intent conditions remain.
Bezer in the wilderness plain is for Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead for Gad, and Golan in Bashan for Manasseh; all three assignments remain.
The law is identified as what Moses set before Israel, beginning the concluding heading.
Testimonies, ordinances and judgments were spoken in the wilderness after Egypt, retaining all three categories.
The heading locates the speech beyond Jordan near Peor in Sihon's land and recalls the defeat after Egypt.
column3: The selected relative pronoun for those struck is plural; inherited whom does not mark number, so its relation to the Amorites rather than only Sihon needs explicit syntactic review.

column2: Both Sihon's and Og's lands are inherited east of Jordan, preserving the two-king scope.
Aroer at Arnon extends to Mount Sion, identified as Hermon; Sion is not treated as Jerusalem's Zion.
All eastern Arabah below Asedoth the hewn height remains, preserving the selected shorter boundary ending without importing a sea clause.
